summary.text: A covalent bond is a chemical bond in which atoms share electrons, forming electron pairs between them.
For many molecules, sharing lets each atom reach the equivalent of a full valence shell, which is a stable electronic configuration.
Sharing can be equal or unequal: atoms with equal electronegativity make nonpolar bonds, while unequal ones make polar bonds.

facts.label: Shared pairs
facts.value: The electron pairs are called shared pairs or bonding pairs

facts.label: Hydrogen sharing
facts.value: Hydrogen atoms share two electrons through covalent bonding

facts.label: Strongest type
facts.value: Sigma bonds are the strongest covalent bonds

facts.label: Double bond makeup
facts.value: One sigma bond and one pi bond

items.prompt: Two hydrogen atoms end up bonded together. What are the atoms doing with their electrons?

options.label: One atom hands its electron over and the two then cling by opposite charge
Each atom keeps its own electron and the nuclei simply attract each other
They share the two electrons, so a pair sits between the atoms
Both electrons are released and drift away from the pair of atoms

items.explain: The hydrogen atoms share the two electrons via covalent bonding. Handing an electron over would be ionic bonding instead.

items.prompt: Which pairing of atoms would make a bond with the most covalent character?

options.label: Two atoms that pull on electrons with similar strength
Two atoms where one pulls on electrons far harder than the other
Two atoms where one is far larger than the other
Two atoms that sit as far apart as the bond allows

items.explain: The covalent character of a bond is greatest between atoms with similar electronegativities, whether or not they are the same element.

items.prompt: In methane, one carbon atom bonds to four hydrogens. How many electrons surround the carbon in that arrangement?
items.explain: Carbon contributes four electrons and the four bonded hydrogens add four more, giving eight (the octet rule).

items.prompt: A chemist says two carbon atoms are joined by a double bond. What is that connection actually made of?

options.label: Two sigma bonds lying side by side
One sigma bond plus one pi bond
Two pi bonds with no sigma bond at all
One sigma bond plus two pi bonds

items.explain: A double bond consists of one sigma and one pi bond. A triple bond has one sigma and two pi bonds.

items.prompt: A molecule has bonds between unequal atoms, yet as a whole it is nonpolar. What could explain this?

options.label: Unequal atoms always share electrons equally once they are bonded
Its bonds must all be sigma bonds, which cannot be polar
Nonpolar molecules form only when the atoms pull with unequal strength
The pulls in different directions cancel out because of its geometry

items.explain: Polarity needs geometric asymmetry. In a symmetric molecule the dipoles can cancel, leaving a non-polar molecule.

items.prompt: Diamond, made of carbon atoms, does not melt until it gets extremely hot. What best explains this?

options.label: Huge numbers of its atoms are linked into one giant 3-dimensional network
Its small separate molecules are held together by weak forces
Its atoms are held together by electrostatic attraction between ions
Its atoms are barely connected, so heat is absorbed slowly

items.explain: Network covalent structures link large numbers of atoms in sheets or 3-dimensional structures like diamond, and such substances have high melting and boiling points.
